hook.text: In 1930, Gandhi walked 240 miles to the sea to make salt illegally.

buildup.text: Britain monopolized salt production in India and taxed every grain sold.

discovery.text: Gandhi picked up natural salt at the shore, breaking the law. Millions followed his example across India.

twist.text: 60,000 Indians were arrested. But the Salt March turned global opinion against British rule.

climax.text: Gandhi proved that defying an unjust tax nonviolently is more powerful than any armed revolt.

punchline.text: One man, one walk, one handful of salt. An empire shook.

quiz.question: How far did Gandhi walk during the Salt March?
